Eudynamys scolopaceus.appearance: Males are glossy blue-black with a pale greenish bill and red eyes. Females are brown with white spots and bars.
Eudynamys scolopaceus.sound: A loud, rising 'ku-oo, ku-oo' repeated again and again, especially in the breeding season.
Eudynamys scolopaceus.fun_fact: Koels lay their eggs in crow nests and leave the crows to raise the chicks.

Acridotheres tristis.appearance: Brown body with a black head, yellow bill, and a bare yellow patch behind the eye. White wing patches show in flight.
Acridotheres tristis.sound: Noisy and chatty, with squeaks, chirps, and gurgles, often calling in groups.
Acridotheres tristis.fun_fact: Common Mynas are very social and gather in large noisy roosts in the evening.

Copsychus fulicatus.appearance: Males are black with a white shoulder patch and a chestnut patch under the tail. Females are brown.
Copsychus fulicatus.sound: A clear, whistling song, often sung from a perch with the tail cocked up.
Copsychus fulicatus.fun_fact: It often holds its tail upright and flicks it while hopping on the ground.

Passer domesticus.appearance: Males have a grey crown and a black bib. Females are plain brown and buff.
Passer domesticus.sound: A simple, repeated cheeping and chirping, often from groups near buildings.
Passer domesticus.fun_fact: House Sparrows live close to people and nest in gaps in walls and roofs.

Psittacula krameri.appearance: A bright green parakeet with a long tail and a red bill. Males have a black and pink ring around the neck.
Psittacula krameri.sound: Loud, sharp, screeching calls, often given in flight.
Psittacula krameri.fun_fact: Flocks gather at dusk to roost together in noisy groups.

Cinnyris asiaticus.appearance: A tiny bird with a thin curved bill. Breeding males look glossy purple-black, while females are olive-brown above and yellowish below.
Cinnyris asiaticus.sound: Sharp, high-pitched 'chwee' notes, repeated in a lively, ringing song.
Cinnyris asiaticus.fun_fact: Sunbirds drink flower nectar and often perch on a flower to feed.
